content:
Arthur P: Heads-up — demo for Nora's prospect in EU-west in 30m, but we're seeing admission-control throttles on the inference cluster. Requests queued and 503s for some routes.
Maya K: Ugh. Which pool? can you paste the error?
Arthur P: Pool eu-west-gpu-pool-1. Logs show `admission_control: rate_limited` and backlog growing. snippet: ```
level=warn msg=\"admission_control: enqueue latency high\" backlog=172 in_flight=64 limit=120
```
Ivan S: That backlog is consistent with the autoscaler not bumping because of quota ceilings. Looks like burst nodes failed at 3:12 UTC with provisioning errors.
Liz G: @ops-oncall can you confirm whether the provisioning failures are due to AZ capacity or our account quota on the cloud side?
ops-oncall: Investigating — initial cloud API calls returning `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for g4dn.xlarge in eu-west-1a. Also seeing 429s on our quota-api when trying to request extra reserved capacity.
Nora (sales): This demo is the EMEA POC with contract review. If we can’t get a soft quota bump they’ll likely pause evaluation. Any possibility of a one-off override? :grimacing:
Maya K: We can do two things: 1) soft-override admission control thresholds for the demo route to allow more queued tokens (risk: latency spikes and possible degraded UX), or 2) route traffic to eu-north or west2 if models and latency are acceptable.
Arthur P: Routing is possible but prospect insisted on eu-west latency. Can we do a temporary quota override while ops works the cloud ticket?
Ivan S: Cloud provider quota team usually needs an org-level approval; can take hours. But we have a short-lived option: spin up smaller instances (more parallel pods) if model fits on a 16GB quantized shard. Cost will spike.
Liz G: If we do that, we need approval from finance for temporary spend cap. Also engineering needs to document rollback plan.
Nora (sales): We can expense the extra for this demo — need a note for the customer explaining we scaled capacity for the trial.
ops-oncall: I pushed a support escalation to the provider at 3:18 UTC, case #CP-97321. They're acknowledging capacity shortage. Meanwhile I can attempt our soft override to admission control for route `/v1/generate/nora-demo`. Need micro-approval.
Maya K: Proposed override: increase per-route concurrent tokens from 120 -> 200 and per-request token cap from 4096 -> 8192 for 2 hours, with circuit breaker to cut at 20% error rate. I can implement and observe.
Arthur P: Approve if finance signs off. @Liz G can you confirm?
Liz G: Approve for 2 hours and cap total spend at $350 for the event. Add alert if projected spend > $300.
Ivan S: I'll prepare the rollback script and a quick metric dashboard: key metrics = backlog, p95 latency, enqueue rate, token-consumption, cost-projection.
support-bot: Action items recorded: `escalation:CP-97321`, `override:route:/v1/generate/nora-demo`, `spend_cap:$350`.
ops-oncall: Rolling the override now — applying patch to admission-control config. Patch: ```
--- admission-config.yaml
+++ admission-config.yaml
@@
-  route: /v1/generate/nora-demo
-    concurrent_tokens: 120
-    max_request_tokens: 4096
+  route: /v1/generate/nora-demo
+    concurrent_tokens: 200
+    max_request_tokens: 8192
+    circuit_breaker: \n+      enabled: true\n+      error_rate_threshold: 0.20
```
Maya K: Watching metrics — backlog is dropping from 172 -> 60 in 3 mins, p95 latency climbed from 210ms -> 560ms but still within demo tolerances?
Nora (sales): Customer sees slightly higher latency but demo is continuing. They asked what happens if we hit errors. I told them we have fallbacks.
Liz G: Finance monitoring shows projected spend for the two-hour window ~ $275. Good. Keep an eye.
Ivan S: Cloud provider just replied: capacity constrained but they expect availability in 6–8 hours for additional instances. So override was necessary.
Arthur P: Can we ensure we mark this as a one-off exception and revert automatically at +2h?
ops-oncall: Yes — auto-revert scheduled at 2 hours after apply. I'll also tag the incident for postmortem and cost reconciliation.
Maya K: Note for postmortem: consider adding a fallback policy that automatically routes to eu-north when instance-type capacity errors surface, to avoid manual overrides.
Arthur P: Thanks team. Nora — please keep us posted if customer wants to run more load or a second demo.
Nora (sales): Will do. Big thanks everyone :pray:
Liz G: Logging action items into the spend and incident trackers.
support-bot: Thread closed for now. Remember to attach postmortem when ready.
